correctness.rationale: The pinned RESULT.md makes a literal, bounded claim about part (v) of Theorem 2.2, not about other clauses. For Omega=[0,1], H=K=K_omega=C with Lebesgue measure, Lambda_omega(z)=z everywhere and Theta_omega(z)=0 at 0, -z otherwise are strongly measurable Parseval continuous g-frames (both squared integrals equal |z|²). As equivalence classes in L2, A(h)=[h] and B(k)=[-k], so their one-dimensional analysis ranges coincide and weak disjointness fails. In contrast Gamma_0(h,k)=h and Gamma_omega(h,k)=h-k off 0, so the literal all-omega kernel is {0}. But Gamma(1,1)=0 a.e.; its L2 analysis kernel is nontrivial. The a.e. correction holds generally because A and B are injective by their frame lower bounds and ker(A+B)={0} iff Ran(A) intersect Ran(B)={0}. Exact independent matrices J_point=[[1,0],[1,-1]] and J_ae=[[1,-1]] have ranks two and one, respectively, with Gram eigenvalues zero and two. Every hypothesis, boundary (exceptional singleton, non-atomic Lebesgue measure), and intended L2 normalization is addressed. Original theorem and proof were checked in full relevant context; no finite sampling extrapolation was used.
residual_risks: If the authors define functions literally without mod-null equivalence, their declared coefficient Hilbert space has zero-norm nonzero vectors; standard L2 interpretation is the mathematically coherent one.

originality.rationale: The specific new statement is a theorem-specific correction and counterexample, not the general fact that L2 functions are defined almost everywhere. The original paper prints a literal all-omega kernel criterion in Theorem 2.2(v) while its proof uses only equality in the Hilbert coefficient space. Fresh checks found no independent erratum or the same singleton witness. Prior discrete g-frame theorems and later continuous-frame operator formulations explain the context but do not state this particular published false-positive and exact repair. The originality judgment is best of knowledge and conditional on the printed literal quantifier.
residual_risks: The source authors may have intended pointwise omega in Omega as informal shorthand for a.e. omega; the exact published display does not say a.e.

value.rationale: This is a narrowly scoped yet mathematically motivated correction of a specifically cited if-and-only-if characterization: a pair of Parseval continuous g-frames satisfies the published kernel test despite failing weak disjointness. The failure makes a claimed decision criterion depend on arbitrary null-set representatives, incompatible with its L2 invariant definition. The exact a.e. repair prevents false positives and supplies a correctly reusable characterization for continuous frame analysis. It is an elementary normalization issue but not an arbitrary cheap type check: it invalidates a stated published theorem under its printed quantifier, identifies the precise logical step and gives a constructive boundary witness. The result does not claim a new general theory or consequences for the other clauses.
residual_risks: Value is limited to a precise corrected theorem statement; if readers already routinely interpret all-omega formulas as a.e., practical impact is smaller.

limitations: Correct only under the literal all-omega reading of the printed theorem; an intended a.e. convention would reduce the discovery to a notation defect.
The theorem-specific diagnosis is limited to Theorem 2.2(v).
Later literature and related 2015 source were checked via abstracts, not full papers; the direct target 2018 paper was read in relevant full-text sections.
